source.name: sp_SharedTempReport

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_SharedTempReport()
RETURNS TABLE (
    OrderDate DATE,
    TotalOrders INT,
    TotalRevenue DECIMAL(12,2)
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- PostgreSQL uses local temporary tables instead of global temp tables
    -- The temp table is session-scoped and will be dropped automatically
    CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS temp_global_order_summary (
        OrderDate DATE,
        TotalOrders INT,
        TotalRevenue DECIMAL(12,2)
    ) ON COMMIT DROP;

    -- Clear any existing data if table already exists
    DELETE FROM temp_global_order_summary;

    INSERT INTO temp_global_order_summary
    SELECT
        CAST(OrderDate AS DATE),
        COUNT(*)::INT,
        SUM(TotalAmount)
    FROM dbo.Orders
    GROUP BY CAST(OrderDate AS DATE);

    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        t.OrderDate,
        t.TotalOrders,
        t.TotalRevenue
    FROM temp_global_order_summary t
    ORDER BY t.OrderDate DESC;

    -- Temp table will be dropped automatically at transaction end
    -- or we can drop explicitly
    DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp_global_order_summary;
END;
$$;
assumptions: Converted global temporary table (##GlobalOrderSummary) to local temporary table (temp_global_order_summary) as PostgreSQL does not have true global temporary tables
The procedure returns a result set, so converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
Assumed dbo.Orders table exists with OrderDate and TotalAmount columns
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL functions don't return row counts by default)
Used ON COMMIT DROP for temp table to ensure cleanup, though explicit DROP is also included
Assumed the function will be called in a way that consumes the result set immediately

reviewFlags.reason: Global temporary tables (##) in SQL Server are visible across sessions, but PostgreSQL temp tables are session-scoped only. If cross-session visibility is required, consider using a permanent application table with session tracking or advisory locks.
reviewFlags.codeSection: CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS temp_global_order_summary

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that the calling application can handle a function returning a table instead of a procedure with a result set. The calling syntax will change from EXEC to SELECT * FROM.
Verify that the dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL and contains the Orders table with the expected columns (OrderDate, TotalAmount). PostgreSQL is case-sensitive with quoted identifiers.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's ##GlobalOrderSummary is visible across all sessions until the creating session ends. PostgreSQL temp tables are session-local only. If multi-session access is needed, use a regular table with session identifiers or implement application-level coordination.
SQL Server: EXEC dbo.sp_SharedTempReport; PostgreSQL: SELECT * FROM dbo.sp_SharedTempReport(); The calling syntax changes from procedure execution to function invocation.

The temp table with ON COMMIT DROP will be dropped at transaction commit. If called outside a transaction block, it drops immediately after the function completes. The explicit DROP may be redundant but ensures cleanup.
SQL Server procedures can return multiple result sets and have OUT parameters. PostgreSQL functions return a single result set. The conversion maintains single result set behavior.
